decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY recording the 3.4V DCDC1 output and its Schottky-drop compensation purpose.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY stating that the power-board input carries the 3.4V DCDC1 output and that the main-board Schottky drop produces the 3.3V system rail.
Changing the normal-operation DCDC1 voltage before power OR-ing does not alter USB enumeration, data routing, connector sourceability, or the USB programming-port role.
The monitored system rail remains 3.3V after the Schottky diodes, so the monitor device, position, rail coverage, and channel allocation remain unchanged.
AXP2101 remains the normal-operation power source for all loads; programming DCDC1 to 3.4V does not change the candidate's battery input or power-path role.
The panel power-button requirement is already introduced by the first clause of the same message, and the DCDC1 voltage decision adds no further change to its connector or control behavior.
The source changes the AXP2101 DCDC1 path for the 3.3V rail and does not change the MT3608 5V boost converter, its enable control, or its loads.
Using I2C to configure DCDC1 does not change the established I2C pull-ups, series resistors, topology, cable assumptions, or bus speed.
The sensor board continues to receive a regulated 3.3V rail from the main board; its connector inventory, pinouts, and fanout remain unchanged.
The new J_PWR_BTN is specified for the power board and does not change the existing main-board panel-control connector inventory or BOOT-button policy.
The SPS30 remains on the 5V supply with the same I2C-mode connector and signals; the DCDC1 3.3V-rail compensation does not affect it.
The addressable LEDs remain powered from 5V with their existing level shifting and separate power control; the DCDC1 compensation change does not alter this interface.
